Bases: object

Class containing the weights for RoutePlanner.eval_function

Parameters:

  • base_cost (float) – The base cost

  • uphill_cost (float) – The cost of an uphill gradient

  • side_gradient_cost (float) – The cost of an sideways gradient

  • downhill_cost (float) – The cost of an downhill gradient

  • relief_cost (float) – The cost of terain relief (maximum change in elevation inside of an (n x n) window)

  • roughness_cost (float) – The cost of terain roughness (standard deviation of the elevation inside an (n x n) window)

  • window_size (int) – The size of the window to evaluate relief and roughness

class main.MinimizeRouteCost(initial_waypoints: ndarray, eval_func: callable, constraints: ndarray, resolution: float, bounds_size: float)[source]¶

Bases: object

Minimize a route’s cost by using the COBYQA minimization algorithm

Parameters:

  • initial_waypoints (np.ndarray) – 2D array of shape (N,2) containing the waypoints of the route to minimize the cost of.

  • eval_func (callable) – A function that accepts (pos, dir) and retruns cost and constrained values. pos and dir are an ndarrays of shape (N,2).

  • constraints (numpy.ndarray) – The maximum values for each constrained variables

  • eval_resolution (float) – The distance between each point when integrating eval_func

  • bounds_size (float) – The size of the boundsfor the minimizer. The minimizer will only evaluate points inside of an (n unit x n unit) window arround the initial waypoints.

class main.RoutePlanner(elevation: ndarray, x: ndarray, y: ndarray)[source]¶

Bases: object

Finds the best route between 2 points on an elevation map

Parameters:

  • elevation (np.ndarray) – 2D array containing the elevation values.

  • x (np.ndarray) – 1D array containing the x coordinates.

  • y (np.ndarray) – 1D array containing the y coordinates.

elevation¶

2D array containing the elevation values. Elevation is transposed, such that x is in the row-wise direction, and y is in the column-wise direction.

Type:

np.ndarray

x¶

1D array containing the x coordinates. x must have constant spacing, and the spacing must be the same with y

Type:

np.ndarray

y¶

1D array containing the y coordinates. y must have constant spacing, and the spacing must be the same with x

Type:

np.ndarray

resolution¶

The spacing between coordinate points.

Type:

float

eval_function(point: ndarray, dir: ndarray, x_grad_interp: RegularGridInterpolator, y_grad_interp: RegularGridInterpolator, relief_interp: RegularGridInterpolator, roughness_interp: RegularGridInterpolator, weights: CostWeights) → tuple[source]¶

Evaluates the cost and constrained values at a point.

Parameters:

  • point (np.ndarray) – 2D array of shape (2,) or 2D array of shape (N,2) containing the point to evaluate the cost and constrained values.

  • dir (np.ndarray) – 2D array of shape (2,N) containing the unit direction vector at each point.

  • x_grad_interp (scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator,) – A RegularGridInterpolator object that returns the gradient in the x direction

  • y_grad_interp (scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator) – A RegularGridInterpolator object that returns the gradient in the y direction

  • relief_interp (scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator) – A RegularGridInterpolator object that returns the terain relief

  • roughness_interp (scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator) – A RegularGridInterpolator object that returns the terain roughness

  • weights (CostWeights) – The weights applied to get the total cost

Returns:

  • cost (float) – The cost at the point. The cost is calculated by the following formula: cost = (base_cost + {uphill_cost if forward gradient is positive, downhill_cost otherwise} * forward_grad + side_gradient_cost * abs(sideways_grad) + relief_cost * relief + roughness_cost * roughness )

  • constrained_vals (numpy.ndarray) – 1D array contining [forward_grad, sideways_grad, -forward_grad, relief, roughness]

find_route(start: ndarray, goal: ndarray, grid_factor: int, heuristics_weight, cost_weights: CostWeights, constraints: ndarray, line_of_sight_optimization: bool = True, minimizer_optimization: bool = False, minimizer_bounds_size: float = 1000, minimizer_max_iter: int = 500, minimizer_constraint_tol: float = 0.0001, minimizer_waypoints_tol: float = 1) → tuple[source]¶

Finds the best route between 2 points through the elevation map

Parameters:

  • start (np.ndarray) – 1D array of shape (2,) containing the starting coordinates

  • goal (np.ndarray) – 1D array of shape (2,) containing the goal coordinates

  • grid_factor (int) – The factor to sample the grid for A* search. A grid_factor of 3 means only 1 every 3 coordinate points in the x and y direction is used, meaning only 1 out of 9 points on the grid are used.

  • heuristics_weight (float) – The weight for the heuristic term h(x) of the A* search

  • cost_weights (CostWeights) – The weights for cost calculation

  • constraints (np.ndarray) – The constraints vector. Can be made using make_constraints_vector()

  • line_of_sight_optimization (bool, optional) – Set to True to apply line of sight optimization (highly recomended). Defaults to True.

  • minimizer_optimization (bool, optional) – Set to True to apply minimizer optimization. Very computationally expensive. Using minimizer optimization without line of sight optimization is not recomended. Defaults to False.

  • minimizer_bounds_size (float, optional) – The size of the boundsfor the minimizer. The minimizer will only evaluate points inside of an (n unit x n unit) window arround the initial waypoints. Defaults to 1000.

  • minimizer_max_iter (int, optional) – Maximum number of iterations for the minimizer algorithm. Defaults to 500

  • minimizer_constraint_tol (float, optional) – Tolarance for the constraints value for the minimizer. Defaults to 1e-4

  • minimizer_waypoints_tol (float, optional) – Tolerance for the final values for waypoints for the minimizer. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

  • waypoints (numpy.ndarray) – ndarray of shape (N,2). Contains the waypoints making up the route if A* search is succesfull. Contains all of the visited cells if A* search is unsuccessfull.

  • cost (float) – The final cost of the route. None if search is unsuccessful.

  • a_star_success_flag (bool) – True if A* search is successfull.

  • minimizer_success_flag (bool) – True if the minimizer successfully converges

main.a_star_search(start: ndarray, goal: ndarray, x: ndarray, y: ndarray, eval_func: callable, eval_resolution: float, constraints: ndarray, heuristic_weight: float, apply_line_of_sight_optimization: bool) → tuple[source]¶

A* search algorithm with line of sight optimization

Parameters:

  • start (numpy.ndarray) – The position to start the search. 1D array of shape (2,) containing the x and y coordinates

  • goal (numpy.ndarray) – The position of the goal. 1D array of shape (2,) containing the x and y coordinates

  • x (numpy.ndarray) – A 1D array containing coordinate points in the x direction.

  • y (numpy.ndarray) – A 1D array containing coordinate points in the y direction.

  • eval_func (callable) – A function that accepts (pos, dir) and retruns cost and constrained values. pos and dir are an ndarrays of shape (N,2).

  • eval_resolution (float) – The distance between each point when integrating eval_func

  • constraints (numpy.ndarray) – The maximum values for each constrained variables

  • heuristic_weight (float) – The weight of the heuristic term h(x)

  • apply_line_of_sight_optimization (bool) – Set to True to apply line of sight optimization

Returns:

  • waypoints (numpy.ndarray) – ndarray of shape (N,2). Contains the waypoints making up the route if search is succesfull. Contains all of the visited cells if unsuccessfull.

  • cost (float) – The final cost of the route. None if search is unsuccessful.

  • success_flag (bool) – True if the search is successfull.

Returns:
